title: Your Delivery Route Becomes a Local-History Radio Station | vitalii.no
description:
I drive the same region every day for work, but tomorrow's stops are never the same route, so any app built around a fixed itinerary breaks by the second day. I wanted to actually learn the places I pass through hundreds of times — in both Norwegian and Ukrainian — without staring at a phone while driving.

guide.vitalii.no is three pieces working together: a harvester that pulls area facts from the local-history wiki, Wikipedia and OpenStreetMap; a VPS runner that turns those facts into short stories with Claude — refusing to write anything without two concrete sourced facts — and voices them with edge-tts in three listening modes (Ukrainian to Norwegian, Norwegian to Ukrainian, and Norwegian only); and a Cloudflare Worker that serves whatever story is ready for the phone's current GPS position. An Android app runs GPS as a foreground service and plays the stories through a simple player, so nothing is bound to a route, only to the area the phone is physically in.

Instead of a route planner, I ended up with a companion that reacts to wherever I am on any given day — and every fact it states traces back to a real published source, never a generated guess, because nothing gets written without two solid sourced facts behind it.
